messages:
sec-scan-bot: CloudScanner detected public-read ACL on bucket redwood-prod-telemetry-logs (us-west-2). finding_id=cs-9876 :eyes:
kyra: ack. linking logs. who owns telemetry infra?
sarah: paging ops-oncall — this bucket has telemetry/traces. severity? possible identifiers?
kyra: low likelihood of PII but need containment asap. public ACLs are unacceptable.
ops-oncall: on it. taking containment. first step: remove public ACL and enable S3 block-public-access.
ops-oncall: running: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-prod-telemetry-logs --acl private` -> OK :white_check_mark:
ops-oncall: applying block: `aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket redwood-prod-telemetry-logs --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true` -> OK
matthew: quick audit: cloudtrail shows `PutBucketAcl` at 2026-03-19T20:14:03Z by principal arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/eks-irsa-redwood-telemetry-role/i-0abc123
kyra: IRSA role for telemetry. likely a pod init container or old automation misconfigured to call PutBucketAcl.
sarah: Ops, can we patch the k8s service account to stop assuming that role while we triage?
ops-oncall: yes. patching SA to remove annotation and restart pods. `kubectl -n telemetry patch sa telemetry-writer -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn":null}}}'` -> rolled, pods restarted.
linda: also need to revoke the role's S3 permissions immediately. propose removing inline policy `telemetry-full-s3`.
matthew: removing inline policy now and replacing with a minimal policy restricted to only PutObject on specific prefixes. `rm inline policy -> done`
linda: rotate any long-lived creds linked to this role. cloudtrail shows assume-role usage only (no access key usage) so likely fine, but confirm no other principals used it.
kyra: KMS check: bucket encrypted with CMK `alias/redwood-telemetry-key`. earlier key policy allowed broad principals. need to tighten.
linda: updating key policy now to restrict to analytics role + bucket principal; removing wildcard entries. applying change.
ops-oncall: added bucket policy deny for public principals as an extra layer. `Deny if Principal == "*" && aws:SourceIp != ...` (simplified) -> applied.
kyra: draft incident comms: what happened, containment actions, scope (which buckets, potential records), and next steps. tagging @product and @security.
sarah: creating follow-up tickets: 1) full scan of S3 buckets for ACL drift vs terraform state 2) infra guardrails to prevent `PutBucketAcl` from CI/CD without review 3) RBAC hardening for IRSA roles with permission boundaries.
matthew: created PR #3125 to tighten `eks-irsa-redwood-telemetry-role` policies and #3126 for terraform enforcement of `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block`. linking them here.
ops-oncall: I'll implement a lambda remediation that runs on CloudWatch Events: if any bucket gets a public ACL, revert ACL + notify in #incidents. will create PR.
kyra: timeline and owners: containment completed in ~12m. ops-oncall (containment), matthew (role policy), linda (KMS policy), sarah (post-incident ticket + comms).
sec-scan-bot: automated re-check at +10m: no public ACL detected for redwood-prod-telemetry-logs. scan_id=cs-9876 -> resolved :white_check_mark:
sarah: thanks all. please add any logs or commands you ran to the ticket. we'll review in a postmortem on Monday and update the S3 runbook to include IRSA checks and KMS policy review.
kyra: recommended post-incident actions (short): [1] account-wide audit for public ACLs and ACL drift, [2] add Terraform/CI guardrail to enforce public access block, [3] require permission boundaries for IRSA roles and ban `s3:*` wildcards, [4] update telemetry init container to avoid altering bucket ACLs and use scoped PutObject, [5] rotate CMK if any suspicious decrypt events appear in next 48h.
sarah: agreed. assigning owners and ETA in ticket. closing Slack thread once monitoring shows no regressions for 24h.
